Method of Attack: Uploading malicious packages to PyPI resembling popular open-source tools
Using a fake Python package mirror (typosquatting) to host poisoned versions of legitimate packages
Hijacking privileged GitHub accounts to alter project files to point to malicious dependencies
Malicious Python code downloads a loader/dropper script that fetches encrypted final payload
Establishing persistence via Windows Registry modification
Stealing browser data, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, Telegram session data, Instagram session tokens, keystrokes, and files from user directories
Uploading stolen data to attacker-controlled servers and anonymous file-sharing services
Impacted Systems: Python development systems using PyPI packages
Windows machines compromised by the malware
Browsers: Opera, Chrome, Brave, Vivaldi, Yandex, Edge
Attack Vector: Supply-chain attack via malicious PyPI packages
Hijacked GitHub maintainer account committing malicious dependencies
Indicators of Compromise: Fake Python package mirror URL: files.pypihosted.org (typosquatting files.pythonhosted.org)
Malicious commits in Top.gg's python-sdk GitHub repository by 'editor-syntax' account
Dependency on poisoned version of 'colorama' package
Use of anonymous file-sharing services: Anonfiles, GoFile
HTTP requests with unique hardware ID and IP address identifiers
